chunks: 4053 - And it is narrated from Abū al-ʿAlāʾ, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man found some money and announced it, until when the year had passed, he bought with it a servant. Then the seeker of the money came and found that the slave-girl whom he had bought with the dirhams was his daughter.

He عليه السلام said: He has no right to take anything except the dirhams, and the daughter is not his. He is only entitled to his principal amount. His daughter had only been the property of some people.

key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمِ: the coins whose value is to be returned
key_terms.السَّنَةُ: the one-year period of announcement for lost property
key_terms.خَادِمًا: a servant purchased with the money
key_terms.رَأْسُ مَالِهِ: his principal amount or original capital
key_terms.فَعَرَّفَهُ: he publicly announced and identified the found property
key_terms.مَالًا: money or wealth that was found
key_terms.مَمْلُوكَةَ: legally owned as property by others

ai.seo_question: If someone buys a slave-girl with found money and the original owner later discovers she is his daughter, does he reclaim the daughter or only the money?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning found property after it has been duly announced for a year and then used in a transaction. If the original owner later appears, he is entitled only to recover the value of his money, not the person purchased with it, even if that person turns out to be his daughter.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4053 - It is narrated from Abu al-Ala, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who found some money, announced it for a year, and then used it to buy a servant. Later, the owner of the money came and found that the servant purchased with the money was actually his daughter.
Imam (as) said: "He is only entitled to take the money and not the daughter. What he is entitled to is his principal amount, as the daughter was previously the property of others."
